sanskrit: tapaḥsvādhyāyanirataṃ tapasvī vāgvidāṃ varam nāradaṃ paripapraccha vālmīkir munipuṃgavam
english: The ascetic Vālmīki questioned Nārada — the foremost among those devoted to austerity and sacred study, the best of the eloquent, the bull among sages.

sanskrit: ko nv asmin sāmprataṃ loke guṇavān kaś ca vīryavān dharmajñaś ca kṛtajñaś ca satyavākyo dṛḍhavrataḥ
english: "Who in this world today is truly virtuous, and also mighty? Who knows righteousness, and is grateful, truthful in speech, and steadfast in his vows?

sanskrit: cāritreṇa ca ko yuktaḥ sarvabhūteṣu ko hitaḥ vidvān kaḥ kaḥ samarthaś ca kaś caikapriyadarśanaḥ
english: Who is endowed with noble character, and who is a benefactor to all creatures? Who is learned, who is capable, and who is ever pleasant to behold?

sanskrit: ātmavān ko jitakrodho dyutimān ko 'nasūyakaḥ kasya bibhyati devāś ca jātaroṣasya saṃyuge
english: Who is self-possessed, who has conquered anger? Who is radiant and free from envy? Whom do even the gods fear when his wrath is aroused in battle?

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me maharṣe tvaṃ samartho 'si jñātum evaṃvidhaṃ naram
english: I wish to hear of such a one — my curiosity is boundless. O great seer, you are capable of knowing such a man."

sanskrit: śrutvā caitat trilokajño vālmīker nārado vacaḥ śrūyatām iti cāmantrya prahṛṣṭo vākyam abravīt
english: Having heard these words of Vālmīki, Nārada — who has knowledge of the three worlds — addressed him saying "Hear me!" and, delighted, spoke thus:

sanskrit: bahavo durlabhāś caiva ye tvayā kīrtitā guṇāḥ mune vakṣyāmy ahaṃ buddhvā tair yuktaḥ śrūyatāṃ naraḥ
english: "The virtues you have enumerated are many and rare, O sage. Having considered them fully, I shall speak of a man who possesses them all — hear of him.

sanskrit: ikṣvākuvaṃśaprabhavo rāmo nāma janaiḥ śrutaḥ niyatātmā mahāvīryo dyutimān dhṛtimān vaśī
english: Born of the lineage of Ikṣvāku, known among men by the name Rāma — he is disciplined in mind, of great valor, radiant, resolute, and master of his senses.

sanskrit: buddhimān nītimān vāgmī śrīmāñ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ vipulāṃso mahābāhuḥ kambugrīvo mahāhanuḥ
english: Intelligent, principled, eloquent, possessed of splendor, a crusher of enemies — broad-shouldered, long-armed, with a neck like a conch-shell and a strong jaw.

sanskrit: mahorasko maheṣvāso gūḍhajatrur ariṃdamaḥ ājānubāhuḥ suśirāḥ sulalāṭaḥ suvikramaḥ
english: Broad-chested, a great archer, with well-concealed collar-bones, a tamer of foes — with arms reaching to his knees, a handsome head, a fine forehead, and noble gait.

sanskrit: samaḥ samavibhaktāṅgaḥ snigdhavarṇaḥ pratāpavān pīnavakṣā viśālākṣo lakṣmīvāñ śubhalakṣaṇaḥ
english: Proportionate, with perfectly balanced limbs, of lustrous complexion, full of majesty — with a full chest, wide eyes, bearing the mark of fortune, adorned with auspicious signs.

sanskrit: dharmajñaḥ satyasaṃdhaś ca prajānāṃ ca hite rataḥ yaśasvī jñānasaṃpannaḥ śucir vaśyaḥ samādhimān
english: Knowing righteousness, true to his pledges, devoted to the welfare of his subjects — illustrious, endowed with wisdom, pure, gracious, and possessed of deep concentration.

sanskrit: rakṣitā jīvalokasya dharmasya parirakṣitā vedavedāṅgatattvajño dhanurvede ca niṣṭhitaḥ
english: A protector of the world of living beings, a guardian of righteousness — one who knows the true essence of the Vedas and their ancillary sciences, and is accomplished in the science of archery.

sanskrit: sarvaśāstrārthatattvajña smṛtimān pratibhānavān sarvalokapriyaḥ sādhur adīnātmā vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: Knowing the true meaning of all treatises, possessed of a retentive memory and swift intelligence — beloved by all the world, virtuous, of undepressed spirit, and discerning.

sanskrit: sarvadābhigataḥ sadbhiḥ samudra iva sindhubhiḥ āryaḥ sarvasamaś caiva sadaikapriyadarśanaḥ
english: Always sought out by the virtuous as the ocean is by rivers — noble, ever impartial toward all, and ever pleasant to look upon.

sanskrit: sa ca sarvaguṇopetaḥ kausalyānandavardhanaḥ samudra iva gāmbhīrye dhairyeṇa himavān iva
english: He, who increases the joy of Kausalyā, is endowed with all virtues — like the ocean in depth, like the Himālaya in steadfastness.

sanskrit: viṣṇunā sadṛśo vīrye somavat priyadarśanaḥ kālāgnisadṛśaḥ krodhe kṣamayā pṛthivīsamaḥ
english: Equal to Viṣṇu in valor, pleasing to behold as the moon — like the fire of universal dissolution in wrath, and like the earth in forbearance.

sanskrit: dhanadena samas tyāge satye dharma ivāparaḥ tam evaṃguṇasaṃpannaṃ rāmaṃ satyaparākramam
english: Equal to Kubera in generosity, a second Dharma himself in truthfulness — him, Rāma, so endowed with virtues, of true valor,

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhaṃ śreṣṭhaguṇair yuktaṃ priyaṃ daśarathaḥ sutam yauvarājyena saṃyoktum aicchat prītyā mahīpatiḥ
english: his eldest son, endowed with the highest virtues, his beloved — king Daśaratha, the lord of the earth, wished out of affection to invest with the office of crown prince.

sanskrit: tasyābhiṣekasaṃbhārān dṛṣṭvā bhāryātha kaikayī pūrvaṃ dattavarā devī varam enam ayācata vivāsanaṃ ca rāmasya bharatasyābhiṣecanam
english: But seeing the preparations for his consecration, his wife Kaikeyī — the queen to whom a boon had previously been granted — asked him for this boon: the banishment of Rāma and the consecration of Bharata.

sanskrit: sa satyavacanād rājā dharmapāśena saṃyataḥ vivāsayām āsa sutaṃ rāmaṃ daśarathaḥ priyam
english: Bound by the snare of righteousness to his word of truth, king Daśaratha sent his beloved son Rāma into exile.

sanskrit: sa jagāma vanaṃ vīraḥ pratijñām anupālayan pitur vacananirdeśāt kaikeyyāḥ priyakāraṇāt
english: The hero went to the forest, honoring his pledge, acting upon his father's command and to please Kaikeyī.

sanskrit: taṃ vrajantaṃ priyo bhrātā lakṣmaṇo 'nujagāma ha snehād vinayasaṃpannaḥ sumitrānandavardhanaḥ
english: His beloved brother Lakṣmaṇa, who increases the joy of Sumitrā, endowed with humility, followed him out of love as he departed.

sanskrit: sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannā nārīṇām uttamā vadhūḥ sītāpy anugatā rāmaṃ śaśinaṃ rohiṇī yathā
english: Sītā too — endowed with all auspicious marks, the foremost of women, the most excellent of daughters-in-law — followed Rāma as Rohiṇī follows the moon.

sanskrit: paurair anugato dūraṃ pitrā daśarathena ca śṛṅgaverapure sūtaṃ gaṅgākūle vyasarjayat
english: Followed for a distance by the citizens and by his father Daśaratha, he dismissed his charioteer at Śṛṅgaverapura on the bank of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: te vanena vanaṃ gatvā nadīs tīrtvā bahūdakāḥ citrakūṭam anuprāpya bharadvājasya śāsanāt
english: Passing through forest after forest, crossing many swift rivers, and reaching Citrakūṭa by the direction of Bharadvāja,

sanskrit: ramyam āvasathaṃ kṛtvā ramamāṇā vane trayaḥ devagandharvasaṃkāśās tatra te nyavasan sukham
english: having built a pleasant dwelling there, the three delighted in the forest and dwelt there happily, resembling gods and Gandharvas.

sanskrit: citrakūṭaṃ gate rāme putraśokāturas tadā rājā daśarathaḥ svargaṃ jagāma vilapan sutam
english: When Rāma had gone to Citrakūṭa, king Daśaratha, tormented by grief for his son and lamenting him, departed to heaven.

sanskrit: mṛte tu tasmin bharato vasiṣṭhapramukhair dvijaiḥ niyujyamāno rājyāya naicchad rājyaṃ mahābalaḥ sa jagāma vanaṃ vīro rāmapādaprasādakaḥ
english: Upon his death, Bharata — of great might — though pressed to accept the kingdom by the twice-born led by Vasiṣṭha, did not desire it. The hero went to the forest to propitiate the feet of Rāma.

sanskrit: pāduke cāsya rājyāya nyāsaṃ dattvā punaḥ punaḥ nivartayām āsa tato bharataṃ bharatāgrajaḥ
english: Rāma, the elder of Bharata, then turned him back, placing his sandals as a pledge for the kingdom.

sanskrit: sa kāmam anavāpyaiva rāmapādāv upaspṛśan nandigrāme 'karod rājyaṃ rāmāgamanakāṅkṣayā
english: Bharata, his wish unfulfilled, touching the feet of Rāma's sandals, administered the kingdom from Nandigrāma, longing for Rāma's return.

sanskrit: rāmas tu punar ālakṣya nāgarasya janasya ca tatrāgamanam ekāgre daṇḍakān praviveśa ha
english: But Rāma, observing the arrival of townsfolk and others to that place, single-mindedly entered the Daṇḍaka forest.

sanskrit: virādhaṃ rākṣasaṃ hatvā śarabhaṅgaṃ dadarśa ha sutīkṣṇaṃ cāpy agastyaṃ ca agastya bhrātaraṃ tathā
english: Slaying the demon Virādha, he visited Śarabhaṅga, then Sutīkṣṇa, then Agastya, and Agastya's brother as well.

sanskrit: agastyavacanāc caiva jagrāhaindraṃ śarāsanam khaḍgaṃ ca paramaprītas tūṇī cākṣayasāyakau
english: At Agastya's word, and greatly pleased, he received the bow of Indra, a sword, and two quivers of inexhaustible arrows.

sanskrit: vasatas tasya rāmasya vane vanacaraiḥ saha ṛṣayo 'bhyāgaman sarve vadhāyāsurarakṣasām
english: While Rāma was dwelling in the forest among the forest-dwellers, all the sages came to him seeking the destruction of the Asuras and Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tena tatraiva vasatā janasthānanivāsinī virūpitā śūrpaṇakhā rākṣasī kāmarūpiṇī
english: While he was dwelling there, Śūrpaṇakhā — a Rākṣasī who dwelt in Janasthāna and could assume any form at will — was disfigured by him.

sanskrit: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhāvākyād udyuktān sarvarākṣasān kharaṃ triśirasaṃ caiva dūṣaṇaṃ caiva rākṣasaṃ
english: Then, at the instigation of Śūrpaṇakhā, all the Rākṣasas rose up — Khara, Triśiras, and the Rākṣasa Dūṣaṇa,

sanskrit: nijaghāna raṇe rāmas teṣāṃ caiva padānugān rakṣasāṃ nihatāny āsan sahasrāṇi caturdaśa
english: Rāma slew them all in battle, along with their followers — fourteen thousand Rākṣasas were destroyed.

sanskrit: tato jñātivadhaṃ śrutvā rāvaṇaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ sahāyaṃ varayām āsa mārīcaṃ nāma rākṣasaṃ
english: Then Rāvaṇa, hearing of the slaughter of his kinsmen and overcome with fury, sought as his ally the Rākṣasa named Mārīca.

sanskrit: vāryamāṇaḥ subahuśo mārīcena sa rāvaṇaḥ na virodho balavatā kṣamo rāvaṇa tena te
english: Mārīca repeatedly warned Rāvaṇa: "Conflict with one so mighty is not fitting for you, O Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: anādṛtya tu tad vākyaṃ rāvaṇaḥ kālacoditaḥ jagāma sahamārīcas tasyāśramapadaṃ tadā
english: But Rāvaṇa, driven onward by fate, disregarded that counsel and went together with Mārīca to Rāma's hermitage.

sanskrit: tena māyāvinā dūram apavāhya nṛpātmajau jahāra bhāryāṃ rāmasya gṛdhraṃ hatvā jaṭāyuṣam
english: That sorcerer, having lured both princes far away, abducted the wife of Rāma, slaying the vulture Jaṭāyus.

sanskrit: gṛdhraṃ ca nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛtāṃ śrutvā ca maithilīm rāghavaḥ śokasaṃtapto vilalāpākulendriyaḥ
english: Finding the vulture slain and hearing that the Maithilī had been carried off, Rāghava was consumed by grief and lamented, his senses overwhelmed.

sanskrit: tatas tenaiva śokena gṛdhraṃ dagdhvā jaṭāyuṣam mārgamāṇo vane sītāṃ rākṣasaṃ saṃdadarśa ha
english: Then, consumed by that very grief, having cremated the vulture Jaṭāyus, he came upon a Rākṣasa while searching for Sītā in the forest.

sanskrit: kabandhaṃ nāma rūpeṇa vikṛtaṃ ghoradarśanam taṃ nihatya mahābāhur dadāha svargataś ca saḥ
english: Named Kabandha, grotesquely misshapen in form and dreadful to behold — him the long-armed hero slew and burned, and he ascended to heaven.

sanskrit: sa cāsya kathayām āsa śabarīṃ dharmacāriṇīm śramaṇīṃ dharmanipuṇām abhigaccheti rāghava so 'bhyagacchan mahātejāḥ śabarīṃ śatrusūdanaḥ
english: Kabandha told him of Śabarī, a female ascetic who walks the path of righteousness, skilled in dharma: "Go to her, O Rāghava." The greatly radiant slayer of enemies then went to Śabarī.

sanskrit: śabaryā pūjitaḥ samyag rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ pampātīre hanumatā saṃgato vānareṇa ha
english: Duly honored by Śabarī, Rāma the son of Daśaratha met on the shore of Pampā with Hanumān, the monkey.

sanskrit: hanumadvacanāc caiva sugrīveṇa samāgataḥ sugrīvāya ca tat sarvaṃ śaṃsad rāmo mahābalaḥ
english: Through Hanumān's words he came to meet Sugrīva, and the mighty Rāma told Sugrīva everything that had befallen him.

sanskrit: tato vānararājena vairānukathanaṃ prati rāmāyāveditaṃ sarvaṃ praṇayād duḥkhitena ca vālinaś ca balaṃ tatra kathayām āsa vānaraḥ
english: Then the king of monkeys, out of affection and sorrow, told Rāma all about the origin of his enmity; and the monkey also recounted there the strength of Vālin.

sanskrit: pratijñātaṃ ca rāmeṇa tadā vālivadhaṃ prati sugrīvaḥ śaṅkitaś cāsīn nityaṃ vīryeṇa rāghave
english: Although Rāma pledged the slaying of Vālin, Sugrīva was always doubtful about Rāghava's valor.

sanskrit: rāghavaḥ pratyayārthaṃ tu dundubheḥ kāyam uttamam pādāṅguṣṭhena cikṣepa saṃpūrṇaṃ daśayojanam
english: To inspire confidence, Rāghava kicked the great carcass of Dundubhi with his toe and hurled it a full ten leagues.

sanskrit: bibheda ca punaḥ sālān saptaikena maheṣuṇā giriṃ rasātalaṃ caiva janayan pratyayaṃ tadā
english: He then pierced seven śāla trees with a single great arrow, penetrating through the mountain down to the netherworld, thereby inspiring conviction.

sanskrit: tataḥ prītamanās tena viśvastaḥ sa mahākapiḥ kiṣkindhāṃ rāmasahito jagāma ca guhāṃ tadā
english: Then, his mind gladdened and his trust secured, the great ape together with Rāma went to the cave of Kiṣkindhā.

sanskrit: tato 'garjad dharivaraḥ sugrīvo hemapiṅgalaḥ tena nādena mahatā nirjagāma harīśvaraḥ
english: Then Sugrīva, the foremost of monkeys, golden-tawny in hue, roared; and at that great roar, the lord of monkeys, Vālin, came forth.

sanskrit: tataḥ sugrīvavacanād dhatvā vālinam āhave sugrīvam eva tad rājye rāghavaḥ pratyapādayat
english: Then, at Sugrīva's word, slaying Vālin in battle, Rāghava reinstated Sugrīva in that kingdom.

sanskrit: sa ca sarvān samānīya vānarān vānararṣabhaḥ diśaḥ prasthāpayām āsa didṛkṣur janakātmajām
english: That bull among monkeys, having assembled all the monkeys, dispatched them in all directions, seeking to find the daughter of Janaka.

sanskrit: tato gṛdhrasya vacanāt saṃpāter hanumān balī śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ pupluve lavaṇārṇavam
english: Then, by the words of the vulture Saṃpāti, the mighty Hanumān leapt across the salt ocean, a hundred leagues in breadth.

sanskrit: tatra laṅkāṃ samāsādya purīṃ rāvaṇapālitām dadarśa sītāṃ dhyāyantīm aśokavanikāṃ gatām
english: Arriving at Laṅkā, the city ruled by Rāvaṇa, he saw Sītā there, lost in thought, situated in the Aśoka grove.

sanskrit: nivedayitvābhijñānaṃ pravṛttiṃ ca nivedya ca samāśvāsya ca vaidehīṃ mardayām āsa toraṇam
english: Having presented the token of recognition, reported all tidings, and consoled the Vaidehī, he demolished the gateway.

sanskrit: pañca senāgragān hatvā sapta mantrisutān api śūram akṣaṃ ca niṣpiṣya grahaṇaṃ samupāgamat
english: Slaying five commanders of the army and seven sons of ministers, and crushing the valiant Akṣa, he was taken captive.

sanskrit: astreṇonmuham ātmānaṃ jñātvā paitāmahād varāt marṣayan rākṣasān vīro yantriṇas tān yadṛcchayā
english: Knowing that the weapon had rendered him senseless by virtue of Brahmā's boon, the hero allowed the Rākṣasas to bind him as they pleased.

sanskrit: tato dagdhvā purīṃ laṅkām ṛte sītāṃ ca maithilīm rāmāya priyam ākhyātuṃ punar āyān mahākapiḥ
english: Having then burned the city of Laṅkā — excepting Sītā the Maithilī — the great ape returned to bring the welcome news to Rāma.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya mahātmānaṃ kṛtvā rāmaṃ pradakṣiṇam nyavedayad ameyātmā dṛṣṭā sīteti tattvataḥ
english: Approaching the great-souled Rāma and circumambulating him, that one of immeasurable spirit declared truthfully: "Sītā has been seen."

sanskrit: tataḥ sugrīvasahito gatvā tīraṃ mahodadheḥ samudraṃ kṣobhayām āsa śarair ādityasaṃnibhaiḥ
english: Then, going with Sugrīva to the shore of the great ocean, he agitated the sea with arrows blazing like the sun.

sanskrit: darśayām āsa cātmānaṃ samudraḥ saritāṃ patiḥ samudravacanāc caiva nalaṃ setum akārayat
english: The ocean, lord of rivers, revealed itself to him; and at the ocean's word he had Nala construct a causeway.

sanskrit: tena gatvā purīṃ laṅkāṃ hatvā rāvaṇam āhave abhyaṣiñcat sa laṅkāyāṃ rākṣasendraṃ vibhīṣaṇam
english: Crossing by that causeway to the city of Laṅkā and slaying Rāvaṇa in battle, he consecrated Vibhīṣaṇa as lord of the Rākṣasas in Laṅkā.

sanskrit: karmaṇā tena mahatā trailokyaṃ sacarācaram sadevarṣigaṇaṃ tuṣṭaṃ rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: By that great deed, the three worlds — with all moving and unmoving things, with all groups of gods and sages — were satisfied with the great-souled Rāghava.

sanskrit: tathā paramasaṃtuṣṭaiḥ pūjitaḥ sarvadaivataiḥ kṛtakṛtyas tadā rāmo vijvaraḥ pramumoda ha
english: Thus honored by all the gods who were supremely pleased, Rāma, his purpose fulfilled and freed from affliction, rejoiced greatly.

sanskrit: devatābhyo varān prāpya samutthāpya ca vānarān puṣpakaṃ tat samāruhya nandigrāmaṃ yayau tadā
english: Having received boons from the gods and raised up the monkeys, he mounted that Puṣpaka vessel and then went to Nandigrāma.

sanskrit: nandigrāme jaṭāṃ hitvā bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito 'naghaḥ rāmaḥ sītām anuprāpya rājyaṃ punar avāptavān
english: At Nandigrāma, having laid aside his matted locks, the sinless Rāma together with his brothers, reunited with Sītā, recovered his kingdom.

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭamudito lokas tuṣṭaḥ puṣṭaḥ sudhārmikaḥ nirāyamo arogaś ca durbhikṣabhayavarjitaḥ
english: The world was filled with joy and delight, contented and well-nourished, deeply righteous — free from ailment and disease, free from the fear of famine.

sanskrit: na putramaraṇaṃ ke cid drakṣyanti puruṣāḥ kva cit nāryaś cāvidhavā nityaṃ bhaviṣyanti pativratāḥ
english: No men anywhere will witness the death of their sons; women will ever be un-widowed and devoted to their husbands.

sanskrit: na vātajaṃ bhayaṃ kiṃ cin nāpsu majjanti jantavaḥ na cāgrijaṃ bhayaṃ kiṃ cid yathā kṛtayuge tathā
english: There will be no fear from wind, no creatures will drown in the waters, no fear from fire — even as it was in the Kṛta age.

sanskrit: aśvamedhaśatair iṣṭvā tathā bahusuvarṇakaiḥ gavāṃ koṭyayutaṃ dattvā vidvadbhyo vidhipūrvakam
english: Having offered hundreds of horse sacrifices and many other rites with abundant gold, and having given ten million cows to the learned in proper observance,

sanskrit: rājavaṃśāñ śataguṇān sthāpayiṣyati rāghavaḥ cāturvarṇyaṃ ca loke 'smin sve sve dharme niyokṣyati
english: Rāghava will establish dynasties of kings a hundredfold, and will set all four orders of society in this world each to its own proper duty.

sanskrit: daśavarṣasahasrāṇi daśavarṣaśatāni ca rāmo rājyam upāsitvā brahmalokaṃ gamiṣyati
english: Having served as king for ten thousand and ten hundred years, Rāma will depart to the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: idaṃ pavitraṃ pāpaghnaṃ puṇyaṃ vedaiś ca saṃmitam yaḥ paṭhed rāmacaritaṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: Whoever recites this story of Rāma — which is pure, destroys sin, meritorious, and equal to the Vedas — is released from all sins.

sanskrit: etad ākhyānam āyuṣyaṃ paṭhan rāmāyaṇaṃ naraḥ saputrapautraḥ sagaṇaḥ pretya svarge mahīyate
english: A man who reads this narrative — the Rāmāyaṇa, which promotes long life — together with his sons and grandsons and his household, is glorified in heaven after death.

sanskrit: paṭhan dvijo vāgṛṣabhatvam īyāt syāt kṣatriyo bhūmipatitvam īyāt vaṇigjanaḥ paṇyaphalatvam īyāj janaś ca śūdro 'pi mahattvam īyāt
english: A Brāhmaṇa who reads it attains mastery of speech; a Kṣatriya attains lordship of the earth; a Vaiśya attains the fruits of his commerce; and even a Śūdra attains greatness.

sanskrit: nāradasya tu tad vākyaṃ śrutvā vākyaviśāradaḥ pūjayām āsa dharmātmā sahaśiṣyo mahāmuniḥ
english: Having heard that speech of Nārada, the great sage, righteous-souled and skilled in speech, honored him together with his disciples.

sanskrit: yathāvat pūjitas tena devarṣir nāradas tadā āpṛṣṭvaivābhyanujñātaḥ sa jagāma vihāyasaṃ
english: Duly honored by him, the divine seer Nārada, taking leave and receiving permission, departed through the sky.

sanskrit: sa muhūrtaṃ gate tasmin devalokaṃ munis tadā jagāma tamasātīraṃ jāhnavyās tv avidūrataḥ
english: A little while after he had departed to the world of the gods, the sage went to the bank of the Tamasā, not far from the Jāhnavī.

sanskrit: sa tu tīraṃ samāsādya tamasāyā mahāmuniḥ śiṣyam āha sthitaṃ pārśve dṛṣṭvā tīrtham akardamam
english: The great sage, reaching the bank of the Tamasā and seeing the ford free of mud, spoke to his disciple who stood at his side:

sanskrit: akardamam idaṃ tīrthaṃ bharadvāja niśāmaya ramaṇīyaṃ prasannāmbu sanmanuṣyamano yathā
english: "Behold, Bharadvāja, this ford free of mud — lovely, its waters clear, like the mind of a good man.

sanskrit: nyasyatāṃ kalaśas tāta dīyatāṃ valkalaṃ mama idam evāvagāhiṣye tamasātīrtham uttamam
english: Set down the water-pot, dear boy, and hand me my bark-garment — I shall bathe here at this excellent ford of the Tamasā."

sanskrit: evam ukto bharadvājo vālmīkena mahātmanā prāyacchata munes tasya valkalaṃ niyato guroḥ
english: Thus addressed by the great-souled Vālmīki, Bharadvāja offered the bark-garment to that sage, attentively, as to a teacher.

sanskrit: sa śiṣyahastād ādāya valkalaṃ niyatendriyaḥ vicacāra ha paśyaṃs tat sarvato vipulaṃ vanam
english: Taking the bark-garment from the disciple's hand, with his senses restrained, he wandered about gazing in all directions at the vast forest.

sanskrit: tasyābhyāśe tu mithunaṃ carantam anapāyinam dadarśa bhagavāṃs tatra krauñcayoś cārunisvanam
english: Then near that spot the blessed one saw a pair of Krauñca birds moving together inseparably, calling with sweet voices.

sanskrit: tasmāt tu mithunād ekaṃ pumāṃsaṃ pāpaniścayaḥ jaghāna vairanilayo niṣādas tasya paśyataḥ
english: Of that pair, a Niṣāda — one resolved on evil, a repository of hatred — struck down the male before the sage's very eyes.

sanskrit: taṃ śoṇitaparītāṅgaṃ veṣṭamānaṃ mahītale bhāryā tu nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā rurāva karuṇāṃ giram
english: The female, seeing her mate slain, writhing on the ground with his limbs drenched in blood, cried out in a piteous voice.

sanskrit: tathā tu taṃ dvijaṃ dṛṣṭvā niṣādena nipātitam ṛṣer dharmātmanas tasya kāruṇyaṃ samapadyata
english: Seeing that bird, a twice-born creature, brought down by the Niṣāda, compassion arose in that righteous-souled sage.

sanskrit: tataḥ karuṇaveditvād adharmo 'yam iti dvijaḥ niśāmya rudatīṃ krauñcīm idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then, from that arising compassion, perceiving this to be unrighteous, hearing the female Krauñca weeping, the twice-born sage spoke these words:

sanskrit: mā niṣāda pratiṣṭhāṃ tvam agamaḥ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ yat krauñcamithunād ekam avadhīḥ kāmamohitam
english: "You shall find no rest, O Niṣāda, for all eternity — for you have slain one of this pair of Krauñca birds while it was in the grip of passion."

sanskrit: tasyaivaṃ bruvataś cintā babhūva hṛdi vīkṣataḥ śokārtenāsya śakuneḥ kim idaṃ vyāhṛtaṃ mayā
english: Even as he spoke thus and reflected, the thought arose in his heart as he looked on: "Moved by grief for this bird, what have I uttered?"

sanskrit: cintayan sa mahāprājñaś cakāra matimān matim śiṣyaṃ caivābravīd vākyam idaṃ sa munipuṃgavaḥ
english: Contemplating this, that greatly wise and intelligent one formed a thought, and that bull among sages spoke these words to his disciple:

sanskrit: pādabaddho 'kṣarasamas tantrīlayasamanvitaḥ śokārtasya pravṛtto me śloko bhavatu nānyathā
english: "This utterance of mine, born of grief, which is composed in metrical feet with equal syllables and suited to the rhythm of the lute — let it be a śloka, and nothing else."

sanskrit: śiṣyas tu tasya bruvato muner vākyam anuttamam pratijagrāha saṃhṛṣṭas tasya tuṣṭo 'bhavad guruḥ
english: His disciple received with great joy that incomparable utterance of the speaking sage; and the teacher was pleased with him.

sanskrit: so 'bhiṣekaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā tīrthe tasmin yathāvidhi tam eva cintayann artham upāvartata vai muniḥ
english: The sage then performed his ablution at that ford according to rule, and returned, his mind still pondering that very meaning.

sanskrit: bharadvājas tataḥ śiṣyo vinītaḥ śrutavān guroḥ kalaśaṃ pūrṇam ādāya pṛṣṭhato 'nujagāma ha
english: Then the disciple Bharadvāja — humble, learned, and obedient to the teacher — took up the full water-pot and followed behind him.

sanskrit: sa praviśyāśramapadaṃ śiṣyeṇa saha dharmavit upaviṣṭaḥ kathāś cānyāś cakāra dhyānam āsthitaḥ
english: He who knows righteousness, entering the hermitage with his disciple, sat down and fell into meditation, while also engaging in various other conversations.

sanskrit: ājagāma tato brahmā lokakartā svayaṃ prabhuḥ caturmukho mahātejā draṣṭuṃ taṃ munipuṃgavam
english: Then Brahmā himself came — the creator of worlds, the self-existent lord, four-faced, of great splendor — to see that bull among sages.

sanskrit: vālmīkir atha taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasotthāya vāg yataḥ prāñjaliḥ prayato bhūtvā tasthau paramavismitaḥ
english: Vālmīki, seeing him, immediately rose, restrained his speech, stood with hands joined, composed and attentive, in utter astonishment.

sanskrit: pūjayām āsa taṃ devaṃ pādyārghyāsanavandanaiḥ praṇamya vidhivac cainaṃ pṛṣṭvānāmayam avyayam
english: He honored that god with water for the feet, an offering of welcome, a seat, and reverential salutation; and prostrating before him according to ritual, he asked after the imperishable one's well-being.

sanskrit: athopaviśya bhagavān āsane paramārcite vālmīkaye maharṣaye saṃdideśāsanaṃ tataḥ
english: The blessed one then sat on the most worshipful seat and assigned a seat to the great seer Vālmīki.

sanskrit: upaviṣṭe tadā tasmin sākṣāl lokapitāmahe tad gatenaiva manasā vālmīkir dhyānam āsthitaḥ
english: When he who is truly the grandsire of all worlds had taken his seat, Vālmīki fell into meditation, his mind still absorbed in that same thought.

sanskrit: pāpātmanā kṛtaṃ kaṣṭaṃ vairagrahaṇabuddhinā yas tādṛśaṃ cāruravaṃ krauñcaṃ hanyād akāraṇāt
english: "What a vile deed was done by that evil-souled one, his mind set on enmity — who without cause killed such a sweet-voiced Krauñca bird!"

sanskrit: śocann eva muhuḥ krauñcīm upaślokam imaṃ punaḥ jagāv antargatamanā bhūtvā śokaparāyaṇaḥ
english: Grieving still for the female Krauñca, his mind turned inward and wholly absorbed in sorrow, he sang that verse again and again.

sanskrit: tam uvāca tato brahmā prahasan munipuṃgavam śloka eva tvayā baddho nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
english: Then Brahmā smiled and said to that bull among sages: "What you have composed is a śloka — there is no doubt about this."

sanskrit: macchandād eva te brahman pravṛtteyaṃ sarasvatī rāmasya caritaṃ sarvaṃ kuru tvam ṛṣisattama
english: "By my will, O Brāhmaṇa, this speech has flowed forth in you. Compose the entire story of Rāma, O best of seers.

sanskrit: dharmātmano guṇavato loke rāmasya dhīmataḥ vṛttaṃ kathaya dhīrasya yathā te nāradāc chrutam
english: Tell the deeds of the righteous-souled, virtuous, wise, and steadfast Rāma as you heard them from Nārada.

sanskrit: rahasyaṃ ca prakāśaṃ ca yad vṛttaṃ tasya dhīmataḥ rāmasya saha saumitre rākṣasānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: What the wise Rāma did — both in private and in public — together with Saumitrī and with all the Rākṣasas in every respect,

sanskrit: vaidehyāś caiva yad vṛttaṃ prakāśaṃ yadi vā rahaḥ tac cāpy aviditaṃ sarvaṃ viditaṃ te bhaviṣyati
english: And what befell the Vaidehī, openly or in secret — all of that which is not yet known shall become known to you.

sanskrit: na te vāg anṛtā kāvye kā cid atra bhaviṣyati kuru rāmakathāṃ puṇyāṃ ślokabaddhāṃ manoramām
english: No word of yours in this poem shall be untrue. Compose the holy story of Rāma, beautiful and bound in śloka meter."

sanskrit: yāvat sthāsyanti girayaḥ saritaś ca mahītale tāvad rāmāyaṇakathā lokeṣu pracariṣyati
english: "As long as the mountains stand and the rivers flow upon the earth, so long will the story of the Rāmāyaṇa circulate throughout the worlds.

sanskrit: yāvad rāmasya ca kathā tvatkṛtā pracariṣyati tāvad ūrdhvam adhaś ca tvaṃ mallokeṣu nivatsyasi
english: As long as the story of Rāma, composed by you, shall circulate, so long shall you dwell in the upper and lower worlds."

sanskrit: ity uktvā bhagavān brahmā tatraivāntaradhīyata tataḥ saśiṣyo vālmīkir munir vismayam āyayau
english: Having said this, the blessed Brahmā vanished then and there. The sage Vālmīki, together with his disciples, was filled with wonder.

sanskrit: tasya śiṣyās tataḥ sarve jaguḥ ślokam imaṃ punaḥ muhur muhuḥ prīyamāṇāḥ prāhuś ca bhṛśavismitāḥ
english: Then all of his disciples sang that śloka again and again with delight, and spoke, greatly astonished:

sanskrit: samākṣaraiś caturbhir yaḥ pādair gīto maharṣiṇā so 'nuvyāharaṇād bhūyaḥ śokaḥ ślokatvam āgataḥ
english: "This grief that was uttered by the great seer in four feet of equal syllables has become a śloka by being sung."

sanskrit: tasya buddhir iyaṃ jātā vālmīker bhāvitātmanaḥ kṛtsnaṃ rāmāyaṇaṃ kāvyam īdṛśaiḥ karavāṇy aham
english: Then this thought arose in Vālmīki, whose spirit was cultivated and purified: "With such verses as these shall I compose the entire Rāmāyaṇa poem."

sanskrit: udāravṛttārthapadair manoramais tadāsya rāmasya cakāra kīrtimān samākṣaraiḥ ślokaśatair yaśasvino yaśaskaraṃ kāvyam udāradhīr muniḥ
english: With hundreds of ślokas of equal syllables, adorned with noble subject-matter and pleasing words — the famous sage of noble intellect composed a glorious poem to the glory of the glorious Rāma.

sanskrit: śrutvā vas tu samagraṃ tad dharmātmā dharmasaṃhitam vyaktam anveṣate bhūyo yad vṛttaṃ tasya dhīmataḥ
english: Having heard all of that — the wholesome account filled with righteousness — the righteous-souled one seeks to see clearly, once more, what befell that wise man.

sanskrit: upaspṛśyodakaṃ saṃyan muniḥ sthitvā kṛtāñjaliḥ prācīnāgreṣu darbheṣu dharmeṇānveṣate gatim
english: The sage, having touched water with restraint, stood with hands joined in salutation, on a cushion of kuśa grass with tips pointing eastward, and by dharma seeks the way.

sanskrit: janma rāmasya sumahad vīryaṃ sarvānukūlatām lokasya priyatāṃ kṣāntiṃ saumyatāṃ satyaśīlatām
english: The great birth of Rāma, his valor, his conformity to all, his belovedness to the world, his patience, his gentleness, his character of truthfulness —

sanskrit: nānācitrāḥ kathāś cānyā viśvāmitrasahāyane jānakyāś ca vivāhaṃ ca dhanuṣaś ca vibhedanam
english: The many and varied other stories in the journey with Viśvāmitra, the marriage of Jānakī, and the breaking of the bow —

sanskrit: rāmarāmavivādaṃ ca guṇān dāśarathes tathā tathābhiṣekaṃ rāmasya kaikeyyā duṣṭabhāvatām
english: The quarrel between Rāma and Rāma, the virtues of Daśaratha's son, the intended consecration of Rāma, and the wicked intent of Kaikeyī —

sanskrit: vyāghātaṃ cābhiṣekasya rāmasya ca vivāsanam rājñaḥ śokavilāpaṃ ca paralokasya cāśrayam
english: The obstruction of the consecration, Rāma's exile, the king's grief and lamentation, and his resort to the other world —

sanskrit: prakṛtīnāṃ viṣādaṃ ca prakṛtīnāṃ visarjanam niṣādādhipasaṃvādaṃ sūtopāvartanaṃ tathā
english: The sorrow of the people, the dismissal of the people, the dialogue with the lord of the Niṣādas, and the turning back of the charioteer —

sanskrit: gaṅgāyāś cāpi saṃtāraṃ bharadvājasya darśanam bharadvājābhyanujñānāc citrakūṭasya darśanam
english: The crossing of the Gaṅgā, the visit to Bharadvāja, and by Bharadvāja's leave the sight of Citrakūṭa —

sanskrit: vāstukarmaniveśaṃ ca bharatāgamanaṃ tathā prasādanaṃ ca rāmasya pituś ca salilakriyām
english: The building and setting up of the dwelling, the arrival of Bharata, the propitiation of Rāma, and the water-rites for the father —

sanskrit: pādukāgryābhiṣekaṃ ca nandigrāma nivāsanam daṇḍakāraṇyagamanaṃ sutīkṣṇena samāgamam
english: The consecration of the sandals as regent, the sojourn at Nandigrāma, the going into the Daṇḍaka forest, and the meeting with Sutīkṣṇa —

sanskrit: anasūyāsamasyāṃ ca aṅgarāgasya cārpaṇam śūrpaṇakhyāś ca saṃvādaṃ virūpakaraṇaṃ tathā
english: The encounter with Anasūyā and the gift of the ointment, the conversation with Śūrpaṇakhā and her disfigurement —

sanskrit: vadhaṃ kharatriśirasor utthānaṃ rāvaṇasya ca mārīcasya vadhaṃ caiva vaidehyā haraṇaṃ tathā
english: The slaying of Khara and Triśiras, the rising up of Rāvaṇa, the slaying of Mārīca, and the abduction of the Vaidehī —

sanskrit: rāghavasya vilāpaṃ ca gṛdhrarājanibarhaṇam kabandhadarśanaṃ caiva pampāyāś cāpi darśanam
english: Rāghava's lamentation, the slaying of the vulture-king, the encounter with Kabandha, and the sight of the Pampā lake —

sanskrit: śarbaryā darśanaṃ caiva hanūmaddarśanaṃ tathā vilāpaṃ caiva pampāyāṃ rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: The visit to Śabarī, the meeting with Hanūmān, and the lamentation of the great-souled Rāghava at Pampā —

sanskrit: ṛṣyamūkasya gamanaṃ sugrīveṇa samāgamam pratyayotpādanaṃ sakhyaṃ vālisugrīvavigraham
english: The going to Ṛṣyamūka, the meeting with Sugrīva, the establishment of trust, the alliance, and the conflict between Vāli and Sugrīva —

sanskrit: vālipramathanaṃ caiva sugrīvapratipādanam tārāvilāpasamayaṃ varṣarātrinivāsanam
english: The destruction of Vālin, the installation of Sugrīva, the pacification of Tārā's lamentation, and the sojourn of the rainy season nights —

sanskrit: kopaṃ rāghavasiṃhasya balānām upasaṃgraham diśaḥ prasthāpanaṃ caiva pṛthivyāś ca nivedanam
english: The wrath of Rāma the lion-hero, the mustering of the troops, the dispatching in all directions, and the description of the earth —

sanskrit: aṅgulīyakadānaṃ ca ṛkṣasya biladarśanam prāyopaveśanaṃ caiva saṃpāteś cāpi darśanam
english: The giving of the signet ring, the sight of the cave of the bears, the sitting in fast unto death, and the appearance of Saṃpāti —

sanskrit: parvatārohaṇaṃ caiva sāgarasya ca laṅghanam rātrau laṅkāpraveśaṃ ca ekasyāpi vicintanam
english: The climbing of the mountain, the leaping of the ocean, the nocturnal entry into Laṅkā, and deliberating alone —

sanskrit: āpānabhūmigamanam avarodhasya darśanam aśokavanikāyānaṃ sītāyāś cāpi darśanam
english: The going to the drinking-ground, the sight of the inner apartments, the going to the Aśoka grove, and the sight of Sītā —

sanskrit: abhijñānapradānaṃ ca sītāyāś cāpi bhāṣaṇam rākṣasītarjanaṃ caiva trijaṭāsvapnadarśanam
english: The presentation of the token of recognition, the conversation with Sītā, the terrifying of the Rākṣasī women, and the dream-vision of Trijaṭā —

sanskrit: maṇipradānaṃ sītāyā vṛkṣabhaṅgaṃ tathaiva ca rākṣasīvidravaṃ caiva kiṃkarāṇāṃ nibarhaṇam
english: Sītā's gift of the jewel, the breaking of the trees, the flight of the Rākṣasī women, and the slaying of the kiṃkara troops —

sanskrit: grahaṇaṃ vāyusūnoś ca laṅkādāhābhigarjanam pratiplavanam evātha madhūnāṃ haraṇaṃ tathā
english: The capture of the son of the Wind-god, his roaring proclamation of Laṅkā's burning, his return voyage, and the plundering of the honey-grove —

sanskrit: rāghavāśvāsanaṃ caiva maṇiniryātanaṃ tathā saṃgamaṃ ca samudrasya nalasetoś ca bandhanam
english: The consolation of Rāghava, the handing over of the jewel, the meeting with the ocean, and the building of Nala's causeway —

sanskrit: pratāraṃ ca samudrasya rātrau laṅkāvarodhanam vibhīṣaṇena saṃsargaṃ vadhopāyanivedanam
english: The crossing of the ocean, the siege of Laṅkā by night, the alliance with Vibhīṣaṇa, and the disclosure of the means of slaying —

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇasya nidhanaṃ meghanādanibarhaṇam rāvaṇasya vināśaṃ ca sītāvāptim areḥ pure
english: The death of Kumbhakarṇa, the slaying of Meghanāda, the destruction of Rāvaṇa, and the recovery of Sītā in the enemy's city —

sanskrit: bibhīṣaṇābhiṣekaṃ ca puṣpakasya ca darśanam ayodhyāyāś ca gamanaṃ bharatena samāgamam
english: The consecration of Vibhīṣaṇa, the sight of the Puṣpaka aerial chariot, the journey to Ayodhyā, and the meeting with Bharata —

sanskrit: rāmābhiṣekābhyudayaṃ sarvasainyavisarjanam svarāṣṭrarañjanaṃ caiva vaidehyāś ca visarjanam
english: The auspicious consecration of Rāma, the dismissal of all the armies, the delighting of his own kingdom, and the sending away of the Vaidehī —

sanskrit: anāgataṃ ca yat kiṃ cid rāmasya vasudhātale tac cakārottare kāvye vālmīkir bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
english: And whatever things of Rāma's yet to come upon this earth — all this the blessed seer Vālmīki composed in the later portion of the poem.
